detail: Product Alpha is conditional; Controlled Pilot, Beta and GA are no-go until real Provider-backed evidence, external release trust and a four-hop run exist.
Repository-local readiness and boundary work is separated from externally owned Provider, Developer ID, SSHSIG and CAS inputs; production composition cannot begin before external verification.

Contracts, projection, mobile reducer and opaque Relay are neutral; connector exports, stock journal storage and supervisor authorization remain OpenCode-specific. Defer broad refactor until a concrete second adapter and begin then with a failing public-surface conformance test.

P0/P1/P2 zero after final-evidence aggregation and provider-name cardinality rework. Ten focused tests and live content-free CLI checks pass; the doctor never executes production, reads secret values or creates authority.

Readiness doctor checks only environment key membership and cardinality; it does not inspect whether a credential value is empty. Credential-value validity remains inside the later single-use real capture boundary.

P0/P1/P2 zero. The doctor checks only fixed local metadata and provider environment key membership, never executes production or reads credential values, and cannot emit production readiness. Ten focused tests pass.

Product plan, architecture dispatch, read-only doctor, operator handoff and agent-boundary audit are complete. No further repository-only task can unlock the Controlled Pilot; resume at externally supplied B1-B5 inputs.

The current executable slice is the localhost-only read-only Host projector to Relay to Gateway to default Mobile UI journey. Pairing, revocation and reply, deny or Stop remain outside this slice and cannot be inferred from local evidence.

A2 may use only POST /v1/frame, token-gated GET /v1/frames and POST /v1/ack for the fixed device. WebSocket, test routes, commands, pairing, production supervisor and Mobile default wiring remain out of scope until their gates.
P0/P1/P2 zero. Alpha ingress rejects even a valid signed frame from a non-fixed registered device before key lookup, signature verification and storage; full and race Relay suites pass.

The first A2-1 callback repeated the completed A1 Relay report and produced no connector diff. The iteration is not counted as progress; the worker was reinjected with explicit owned files, contracts and tests.

Early cross-review caught divergent 64 KiB versus 256 KiB bounds, incompatible event and change shapes, and a Host-side premature gateway_schema_verified claim. Freeze is withheld while the architect resolves one honest wire-to-API contract.

Host wire uses nomad.alpha.readonly.host.v1 with false verification flags, safe metadata aliases and unavailable changes. Gateway validates and durably stores the Host record before ACK, then derives nomad.alpha.readonly.v1 with true verification flags and a new digest.

Full Cargo initially exposed fixed-port competition and a leaked fake OpenCode child between integration binaries. Both suites now coordinate with a shared OS flock and each lease owns and cleans its process before releasing the lock; two full Cargo runs and clippy pass.

Gateway mechanics pass focused review, but the default browser still targets /api/pilot routes. Keep the finding open as the planned A3 dependency until the UI uses /api/alpha/session and removes write controls.

A2 remains unfrozen: Host payload bytes were not canonical, Rust generation admitted values rejected by the JS schema, and no real Go Relay plus Rust projector plus JS Gateway process proof existed. Projector parity and a dedicated content-free multiprocess runner were dispatched.

Canonical Host wire bytes, strict Rust generation validation and a real Go Relay plus Rust projector plus JS Gateway restart runner now pass. Independent A2 re-audit is in progress; the source remains explicitly synthetic and confers no Pilot or production readiness.

Default Alpha routing and read-only controls are correct, but valid unavailable and unknown states were collapsed into schema errors and UI classification guessed from error text. A typed availability path was returned for rework before browser validation.

P0/P1/P2 zero after canonical wire, strict Rust generation validation, real Go Relay signature path and real Rust projector plus JS Gateway restart evidence. This is local mechanics over a synthetic source, not Pilot or production evidence.
Pre-browser review found that a refresh failure could leave a previously Live view rendered below the error. A3 was reopened to clear stale view state before browser acceptance.

Headless Chrome exposed concurrent default Alpha GETs from React StrictMode. Concurrent BEGIN IMMEDIATE calls on one SQLite connection could produce 503 unavailable despite a durable projection. Gateway was reopened for per-server single-flight ingestion and a concurrent-request regression test.

Real headless Chrome loaded the default non-mock read-only UI through the Rust projector, Go Relay and JS Gateway. Default Alpha requests were one, Pilot requests and Relay test routes were zero, write controls were absent, and Relay loss cleared the previous Live view. Source remained SYNTHETIC_SOURCE and Pilot and production readiness remained false.

A1, A2 and A3 independent reviews and final browser acceptance report no P0/P1/P2 findings for the localhost read-only Alpha slice. The result does not include pairing, revocation, commands, real Provider evidence, production trust, or Controlled Pilot readiness.

The next gate is no longer repository-local feature work. Controlled Pilot remains blocked on one allowlisted real Provider run and lifecycle evidence, Developer ID Host, external SSHSIG trust and KRL, protected CAS publication, locked official OpenCode evidence, and native production supervisor composition.
